findings.statement: deferred consolidation lifts fragmenting append throughput
findings.detail: deferred 160434 ops/s against inline 140817 (deferred vs inline: greater 1.139x (p=0.0122, rel_iqr 1.2%/2.5%)); the inline arm merged 30000 times where the deferred arm merged 24000

findings.statement: deferred consolidation shortens the append latency tail
findings.detail: append p99.9: inline 116.7us, deferred 106.0us (inline_p999 vs deferred_p999: NO DIFFERENCE (ratio 1.101, p=0.0947) -- within noise, not a result); worst single append 15.07ms against 17.61ms. This is F5.1's tail, measured against the policy that causes it

findings.statement: deferred consolidation does not slow the read-back pass
findings.detail: read-back at 12.937 Mvalues/s deferred against 21.360 inline (deferred vs inline: less 0.606x (p=0.0122, rel_iqr 1.4%/2.8%)). The deferred arm walks O(threshold + log n) extents per key where inline walks at most threshold, and this is what that costs

findings.statement: deferred consolidation sends fewer bytes to the device
findings.detail: inline 135.1 MB to the block layer against deferred 107.6 for 10.6 MB of appended records (inline_mb vs deferred_mb: greater 1.255x (p=0.0040, rel_iqr 0.0%/0.0%)). The O(n^2) rewrite is a device cost before it is a latency cost, which is how W1.3 saw it first

findings.statement: deferred consolidation does not grow the file
findings.detail: file after close: deferred 107.72 MB against inline 135.65 (deferred_mb vs inline_mb: less 0.794x (p=0.0040, rel_iqr 0.0%/0.0%))

notes: both arms interleaved in one process; the only difference is Options::defer_merge
line-ordered appends: every key's run is broken by every other key's, so every key fragments and the merge policy is the thing under load -- the shape W1.3 prices at 18.08x on the space axis
peak RSS is process-wide and the arms share the process, so it is reported once and bounds both
